cards.explanation: The answer is pray for them. The LORD tells Jeremiah, the prophet, “As for you, do not pray for these people…” (Jeremiah 7:16). Then He adds, “…for I will not listen to you.” I bet that was a hard thing for a prophet to hear, friends.
The answer is False, friends. The LORD says, “…do not beg Me, for I will not listen to you.” (Jeremiah 7:16). He doesn't say He'll listen if Jeremiah begs anyway. He says He won't.

The answer is cakes for the Queen of Heaven. The text says “…the women knead the dough to make cakes for the Queen of Heaven…” (Jeremiah 7:18). The sons gather wood and the fathers light the fire, so the whole family has a part. It's a heavy thing to read, friends.

The answer is to provoke Him to anger. The LORD says they “…pour out drink offerings to other gods to provoke Me to anger.” (Jeremiah 7:18). He gives the reason Himself. That's all we need to know about why.

The answer is themselves. The LORD asks, “But am I the One they are provoking?… Is it not themselves they spite, to their own shame?” (Jeremiah 7:19). It's a question that makes you stop and think, friends. Shame lands on the ones doing it.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD says His anger and fury will be poured out on this place, “…and it will burn and not be extinguished.” (Jeremiah 7:20). The verse says the fire will not be put out. It's a serious line, so let's just let it sit.

The answer is that they should eat it themselves. The LORD of Hosts says, “Add your burnt offerings to your other sacrifices and eat the meat yourselves!” (Jeremiah 7:21). A burnt offering is the kind that went up on the altar whole (Leviticus 1:9). So being told to eat the meat of it, friends, is a startling thing to hear.

The answers are God and people. The LORD says, “Obey Me, and I will be your God, and you will be My people.” (Jeremiah 7:23). The first half of that promise is about who He will be, and the second half is about who they will be. Everything else in that verse hangs on it, friends.

The answer is False, friends. The LORD says they followed the stubborn inclinations of their own evil hearts, and “They went backward and not forward.” (Jeremiah 7:24). So the fathers went backward, and forward isn't what the verse says.

The answer is again and again. The LORD says, “…I have sent you all My servants the prophets again and again.” (Jeremiah 7:25). That covers the whole stretch from Egypt until that day. It was more than one try, friends.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD says they would not listen to Him or incline their ear, “…but they stiffened their necks and did more evil than their fathers.” (Jeremiah 7:26). It's a heavy verse. It follows right after the fathers' own story.

The answer is that they will not listen to him. The LORD tells Jeremiah, “When you tell them all these things, they will not listen to you.” (Jeremiah 7:27). That's a tough assignment, friends. He's told ahead of time how it will go.

The answer is perished, friends. The message says, “Truth has perished; it has disappeared from their lips.” (Jeremiah 7:28). It's the same sad point in two phrases. That's said about the nation that would not listen to the voice of the LORD their God.

The answer is that the LORD has rejected that generation. The message says, “…for the LORD has rejected and forsaken the generation of His wrath.” (Jeremiah 7:29). That's the reason given for the lament, friends. It's a heavy line.

The answer is defiled. The LORD says they “…set up their abominations in the house that bears My Name, and so have defiled it.” (Jeremiah 7:30). The house that bears His Name is the one that was defiled.

The answer is the Valley of Slaughter. The LORD says it will no longer be called Topheth and the Valley of Ben-hinnom, “…but the Valley of Slaughter.” (Jeremiah 7:32). The reason He gives is that they will bury the dead in Topheth until there is no more room. This is a heavy one, friends.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD says the corpses will become food for the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth, “…and there will be no one to scare them away.” (Jeremiah 7:33). It's a hard picture. I think the quiet in it is part of what makes it heavy.

The answer is that the land will become a wasteland. The LORD says He will remove the sounds of joy and gladness and the voices of the bride and bridegroom, “…for the land will become a wasteland.” (Jeremiah 7:34). That's the reason the verse gives, friends. I think it's a sad picture.

The answer is loved and served them, friends. The host of heaven are what “…they have loved, served, followed, consulted, and worshiped.” (Jeremiah 8:2). The text gives a whole list, and loved and served are on it. The LORD says the bones will be exposed to the sun and moon and all the host of heaven.

The answer is False, friends. The LORD says, “Their bones will not be gathered up or buried, but will become like dung lying on the ground.” (Jeremiah 8:2). They stay out in the open. It's a hard picture.
The answer is death, friends. The LORD of Hosts says, “…the remnant of this evil family will choose death over life…” (Jeremiah 8:3). It's a sobering line to end on. That's the word in the blank.
